usage: The plain present-tense statement, the same for men and women. Use it when you cannot follow in general; for something that was just said, the past form lam afham is more natural. Pairing it with a request to repeat or slow down keeps the conversation going.

variants.label: about what was just said
variants.note: Use right after a sentence you missed.

variants.label: about your Arabic
variants.english: I do not understand Arabic well
variants.note: Use to set expectations at the start.

variants.label: asking to repeat, to a man
variants.note: Use when you want the sentence again.

variants.label: asking to slow down, to a man
variants.note: Use when the speed is the problem.

examples.english: Sorry, I do not understand this word.
I don't understand, do you speak English?

examples.arabic: لَا أَفْهَمُ السُّؤَالَ، أَعِدْهُ مِنْ فَضْلِكَ.
examples.transliteration: la afhamu as-su'ala, a3idhu min fadlika.
examples.english: I don't understand the question, please repeat it.
